1	# Structural BPMN (what the registry does not emit)
2	
3	The registry's `xmlTemplate`s give you the `uipath:*` payload for each node
4	(see [registry-workflow.md](registry-workflow.md)). They do **not** give you the
5	structural BPMN that holds those nodes together. This file is the ground truth
6	for everything you author by hand around the templates.
7	
8	Two sources define the contract:
9	
10	- the registry spec `bpmn-spec.json` — enumerates which BPMN element types and
11	  event definitions exist, via its `bpmnElements` section;
12	- the Studio Web canvas serializer
13	  (`PO.Frontend/src/services/serialization/`) — defines how that XML must be
14	  shaped to import and round-trip.
15	
16	Where the registry stops, the canvas serializer is authoritative. Each
17	gap below is labelled **REGISTRY GAP** — the registry exposes no template for
18	it, so author it from this reference.
19	
20	BPMN XML element names are case-sensitive. Use the exact lower-camel BPMN tag
21	names the serializer emits, such as `<bpmn:startEvent>`,
22	`<bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent>`, `<bpmn:scriptTask>`, and `<bpmn:endEvent>`.
23	Do not use PascalCase variants like `<bpmn:IntermediateCatchEvent>`; XML accepts
24	them syntactically, but BPMN tools do not treat them as the same elements.
25	
26	## The document scaffold (REGISTRY GAP)
27	
28	The registry emits no `<bpmn:definitions>` / `<bpmn:process>` root and no
29	namespace declarations. Author this shell yourself. The canvas import detector
30	(`exporter.ts`) requires: a root `<…:definitions>` carrying a BPMN-spec
31	namespace, at least one `<bpmn:process>`, and (to render) a
32	`<bpmndi:BPMNDiagram>`.
33	
34	```xml
35	<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
36	<bpmn:definitions
37	    xmlns:bpmn="http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/MODEL"
38	    xmlns:bpmndi="http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/DI"
39	    xmlns:dc="http://www.omg.org/spec/DD/20100524/DC"
40	    xmlns:di="http://www.omg.org/spec/DD/20100524/DI"
41	    xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
42	    xmlns:uipath="http://uipath.org/schema/bpmn"
43	    id="Definitions_1" targetNamespace="http://bpmn.io/schema/bpmn"
44	    exporter="UiPath (https://bpmn.uipath.com)" exporterVersion="1.0">
45	  <bpmn:process id="Process_1" isExecutable="true">
46	    <!-- variables, flow nodes, sequence flows -->
47	  </bpmn:process>
48	  <bpmndi:BPMNDiagram id="Diagram_1">
49	    <bpmndi:BPMNPlane id="Plane_1" bpmnElement="Process_1">
50	      <!-- one BPMNShape per node, one BPMNEdge per flow -->
51	    </bpmndi:BPMNPlane>
52	  </bpmndi:BPMNDiagram>
53	</bpmn:definitions>
54	```
55	
56	The `uipath:` namespace URI is exactly `http://uipath.org/schema/bpmn`. All
57	`uipath:*` tags inside `extensionElements` are lower-camelCase
58	(`uipath:activity`, `uipath:variables`, `uipath:loopCharacteristics`, …).
59	
60	Every `uipath:activity` / `uipath:event` / `uipath:mapping` carries its node
61	type as a **child** element — `<uipath:type value="<Type>" version="v1" />` —
62	never as a `type=` attribute on the wrapper. This holds both for templated nodes
63	and for any shell you author or preserve by hand.
64	
65	XML comments must not contain `--` (double-hyphen): it is invalid XML and the
66	file will fail to parse. Never paste CLI commands or flags
67	(`--output`, `--connection-id`) into `<!-- … -->`. Keep comments minimal.
68

138	
139	## Variables (`BPMN.Variables`)
140	
141	Declare root variables with the `BPMN.Variables` registry template attached to
142	the process via `extensionElements`, or use the canvas `<uipath:variables>`
143	block directly. Variable bodies are CDATA. Reference variables in expressions as
144	`vars.<id>` — see [expression-authoring.md](expression-authoring.md).
145	Sub-process-scoped variables go in that sub-process's own `<uipath:variables>`.
146	For a value produced only by a task output, prefer root
147	`<uipath:output id="..." name="..." type="..." />`; preserve the exact id and
148	target that same id from `uipath:output var="..."`.
149	
150	## Script tasks (`BPMN.ScriptTask`) — Jint runtime contract
151	
152	`bpmn:scriptTask scriptFormat="JavaScript"` runs under **Jint**, not Node.js or
153	a browser. The mapping payload comes from the `BPMN.ScriptTask` registry
154	template, but the runtime contract is fixed:
155	
156	- Only these helpers exist: `uipath.aggregate`, `uipath._aggregate`,
157	  `uipath._pipe`, and a no-op `console`. No npm packages, filesystem, network,
158	  browser globals, or long-running async behavior. Execution envelope is ~64 MB
159	  / 30 s.
160	- Set `uipath:scriptVersion value="v3"` for new scripts; preserve an imported
161	  `value="v2"`. For v2+ the script returns JSON under `response`.
162	- Mapped `args` fields are read as **top-level identifiers** in the script body
163	  (`amount`, not `args.amount`); the input mapping itself stays `name="args"`
164	  with `type="json"` and `target="bodyField"`, and maps each field by variable
165	  id (`=vars.Var_Amount`). Include `<uipath:input name="args" type="json"
166	  target="bodyField"><![CDATA[{}]]></uipath:input>` even when there are no
167	  inputs; this is part of the `BPMN.ScriptTask` registry template.
168	- Map the returned object's property back through `source="=result.response"`
169	  (the conventional scalar property) or `source="=result.response.<field>"`
170	  (another object field); `var` points at a declared variable id (do not put the
171	  target id in `name`).
172	- When the output mapping uses `source="=result.response"`, return an object
173	  with a `response` property, such as `return { response: 6 * 7 };`. Do not
174	  return the bare primitive `42` for that mapping shape; there is no
175	  `response` property to bind, so the runtime variable stays empty.
176	- Do not use `source="=result"` with a bare scalar return in live debug/runtime
177	  BPMN. Studio Web can report `FinalStatus: Completed` while the target root
178	  variable still reads back as `{}` or `null` from
179	  `debug-instance variables-all`.
180	- For live debug/runtime runs, never use `source="=this.result"` or
181	  `<uipath:type value="BPMN.Variables" ...>` on a script task output mapping.
182	  That older structural-test shape can pass local validation but leaves root
183	  variables `null` or faults in Studio Web. Use the `BPMN.ScriptTask` mapping
184	  with `source="=result.response"`.
185	- Do not mutate `Globals.*`, `vars.*`, or process variables inside the script
186	  body. The supported path is: return a value from the script, then use a
187	  `uipath:output` mapping to write it to the declared variable. Direct mutation
188	  is not applied to the runtime, so the variable reads empty afterward.
189	
190	```xml
191	<bpmn:scriptTask id="Task_RiskScore" name="Risk Score" scriptFormat="JavaScript">
192	  <bpmn:extensionElements>
193	    <uipath:scriptVersion value="v3" />
194	    <uipath:mapping version="v1">
195	      <uipath:type value="BPMN.ScriptTask" version="v1" />
196	      <uipath:input name="args" type="json" target="bodyField"><![CDATA[{"amount":"=vars.Var_Amount","daysOverdue":"=vars.Var_DaysOverdue"}]]></uipath:input>
197	      <uipath:output name="riskScore" type="number" var="Var_RiskScore" source="=result.response" />
198	    </uipath:mapping>
199	  </bpmn:extensionElements>
200	  <bpmn:script><![CDATA[
201	var score = amount * 0.01 + daysOverdue * 2;
202	return { response: score };
203	]]></bpmn:script>
204	</bpmn:scriptTask>
205	```
206	
207	## Sequence flows, conditions, and gateway defaults (REGISTRY GAP)
208	
209	The registry never emits `<bpmn:sequenceFlow>`, conditions, or the gateway
210	`default` attribute. Author all of them.
211	
212	- A flow: `<bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_1" sourceRef="A" targetRef="B" />`. The
213	  source/target nodes must also list `<bpmn:incoming>`/`<bpmn:outgoing>`
214	  (the registry templates leave `{incomingEdge}`/`{outgoingEdge}` placeholders
215	  for exactly these).
216	- Conditional flow body: `<bpmn:conditionExpression xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression">=vars.Var_X == "approved"</bpmn:conditionExpression>`.
217	  The canvas normalizes the body to start with `=` — always lead with `=`.
218	- Gateway default flow: set `default="Flow_else"` on the gateway element, and
219	  give that flow no condition.
220	
221	## Gateways
222	
223	Author these gateway types for new BPMN: `bpmn:ExclusiveGateway`,
224	`bpmn:ParallelGateway`, `bpmn:InclusiveGateway`, `bpmn:EventBasedGateway`.
225	`bpmn:ComplexGateway` round-trips structurally but is **preserve-only** — do not
226	generate it for new authoring (see [Do not generate for new
227	authoring](#do-not-generate-for-new-authoring-preserve-on-round-trip-only)).
228	
229	- **Exclusive (XOR)**: each non-default outgoing flow needs a
230	  `conditionExpression`; exactly one outgoing flow is the `default`. (Validator
231	  rule `MISSING_CONDITION_EXPRESSION`.)
232	- **Parallel (AND)**: fork = one in, many out; join = many in, one out. No
233	  conditions.
234	- **Inclusive (OR)**: conditions on outgoing flows; multiple may be taken.
235	- **Event-based**: routes to the first of several catch events / receive tasks
236	  to fire; its outgoing flows target intermediate catch events or receive tasks.
237	- A gateway with exactly one incoming and one outgoing flow is rejected
238	  (`SUPERFLUOUS_GATEWAY`). Activities/events must not have more than one
239	  incoming flow — join with a gateway, not a "fake join" (`FAKE_JOIN`).
240	
241	## Events and the event-definition matrix
242	
243	`bpmn-spec.json` `bpmnElements.events` enumerates which event definitions each
244	event element can carry on **round-trip**. For **new authoring**, only the
245	**none**, **Message**, **Timer**, **Error** (on end + boundary), and
246	**Terminate** (on end events only) definitions are generated. Conditional,
247	Signal, Escalation, Compensate, Cancel, Link, multiple, and parallel-multiple
248	definitions are **preserve-only** — keep them when imported, but do not generate

277	  `bpmn:extensionElements`, and a sibling `<bpmn:messageEventDefinition />`.

286	  `<bpmn:terminateEventDefinition />`.

299	### Boundary events (REGISTRY GAP for `attachedToRef` / `cancelActivity`)
300	
301	A boundary event attaches to an activity and catches an event on it. The
302	registry exposes no boundary template; author it:
303	
304	```xml
305	<bpmn:boundaryEvent id="Boundary_Timeout" attachedToRef="Task_DoWork" cancelActivity="true">
306	  <bpmn:timerEventDefinition>
307	    <bpmn:timeDuration xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression">PT15M</bpmn:timeDuration>
308	  </bpmn:timerEventDefinition>
309	  <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_OnTimeout</bpmn:outgoing>
310	</bpmn:boundaryEvent>
311	```
312	
313	- `attachedToRef` = id of the activity it sits on. The boundary event and that
314	  activity must be `flowElements` of the same parent scope.
315	- `cancelActivity="true"` = interrupting (default); `cancelActivity="false"` =
316	  non-interrupting. Per the spec, non-interrupting is available for
317	  Message/Timer/Escalation/Conditional/Signal — **not** Error or Compensate.
318	- Only one catch-all (no `errorRef`) error boundary event per task, and no two
319	  error boundary events with the same error code on one task
320	  (`MULTIPLE_CATCH_ALL_BOUNDARY_EVENTS_ON_TASK`,
321	  `DUPLICATE_ERROR_BOUNDARY_EVENT_ON_TASK`).
322	
323	### Retry and error mapping (REGISTRY GAP)
324	
325	UiPath-specific retry and error-mapping metadata live inside an activity's
326	`extensionElements`. The error **code** lives on the declared
327	`bpmn:error errorCode="…"`; `uipath:*` elements reference it through `errorRef`.
328	
329	```xml
330	<uipath:retry maxRetryCount="2" retryBackoff="PT30S" retryBackoffType="exponential"
331	              maxDuration="PT5M" exponentialBase="2" retryAllErrors="false">
332	  <uipath:errorDefinition errorRef="Error_ServiceUnavailable" />
333	</uipath:retry>
334	<uipath:errorMapping version="v1">
335	  <uipath:error id="Mapped_ServiceUnavailable" errorRef="Error_ServiceUnavailable"
336	                priority="1" condition="=vars.error.code == "SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE""
337	                detail="Service unavailable" retryable="true" />
338	</uipath:errorMapping>
339	```
340	
341	- `uipath:retry` attributes: `maxRetryCount`, `retryBackoff`, `retryBackoffType`,
342	  `maxDuration`, `exponentialBase`, `retryAllErrors`. Do not use stale aliases
343	  (`maxAttempts`, `interval`).
344	- `uipath:error` (mapping) fields: `id`, `errorRef`, `priority`, `condition`,
345	  `detail`, `retryable` (`true`/`false`). Conditions read the runtime error via
346	  `vars.error` and contain no assignments. Do not put `code=` on `uipath:error`;
347	  model the code on `bpmn:error errorCode` and reference via `errorRef`.
348	
349	## Subprocess, call activity, event subprocess (REGISTRY GAP for structure)
350	
351	- **SubProcess** (`bpmn:SubProcess`): a container with its own nested
352	  `flowElements` (start event, nodes, end event) and its own scoped
353	  `<uipath:variables>`. Variants: `collapsed`, `expanded`, `eventSubprocess`.
354	  The shape carries `isExpanded` for the collapsed/expanded distinction.
355	- **Event subprocess**: a `bpmn:SubProcess` with `triggeredByEvent="true"`. It
356	  must have **exactly one** start event, and that start event **must carry an
357	  event definition** (with `isInterrupting`) — a blank start event is invalid for
358	  an event subprocess.
359	- **Call activity** (`bpmn:CallActivity`): invokes a *separate* Maestro
360	  instance. The registry provides the `uipath:activity` payload for the
361	  Orchestrator agentic/case-management call-activity types
362	  (`Orchestrator.StartAgenticProcess[Async]`, `…CaseMgmtProcess[Async]`). A
363	  plain BPMN `calledElement` round-trips but is not specially authored by the
364	  canvas layer.
365	- Each scope (process or sub-process) may have at most one blank (untyped) start
366	  event (`MULTIPLE_BLANK_START_EVENTS`).
367	
368	> SubProcess scopes operations *within the same instance*; CallActivity invokes
369	> a *separate* Maestro instance. Do not conflate them.
370	
371	## Multi-instance / loop characteristics (REGISTRY GAP — canvas supports it)
372	
373	The registry spec enumerates **no** multi-instance or loop markers
374	(`grep` for `multiInstance`/`loopCharacteristics` in `bpmn-spec.json` returns
375	nothing). This is a genuine registry gap. The Studio Web canvas, however, **does**
376	serialize them (`elements/nodes.ts`), so author them from the canvas contract:
377	
378	```xml
379	<bpmn:multiInstanceLoopCharacteristics isSequential="true">
380	  <bpmn:completionCondition xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression">=vars.Var_Done</bpmn:completionCondition>
381	  <bpmn:extensionElements>
382	    <uipath:loopCharacteristics
383	        inputCollection="=vars.Var_Items" inputElement="item" />
384	  </bpmn:extensionElements>
385	</bpmn:multiInstanceLoopCharacteristics>
386	```
387	
388	- `isSequential="true"` = one at a time; `false` = parallel.
389	- The collection/item binding lives in the `uipath:loopCharacteristics`
390	  extension (`inputCollection`, `inputElement`), **not** in `loopCardinality`
391	  (the canvas never reads `loopCardinality`).
392	- The loop element **must declare `inputElement`** — do not rely on reading a
393	  bare `iterator`/`iterator.item` downstream without it. For a multi-instance
394	  **subprocess** body, bind `inputElement="iterator[0]"` on
395	  `uipath:loopCharacteristics` and pass the current item into body activities
396	  with `=iterator[0].item`. Do not assume a bare alias such as `=currentItem` is
397	  in scope inside a marker subprocess body unless the file already uses it.
398	- Inside the body, read the current item with the `iterator` namespace — see
399	  [expression-authoring.md](expression-authoring.md).
400	- `bpmn:standardLoopCharacteristics` is also recognized (no uipath extension).
401	
402	Because the registry exposes no template for this, treat it as a documented
403	authoring path backed by the canvas serializer, and tell the user it is a
404	registry gap if they ask why no `registry get` covers it.

451	## Diagram interchange — `bpmndi` (REGISTRY GAP — always generated)
452	
453	The registry emits no diagram. Import is **diagram-driven**: the canvas builds
454	nodes from `BPMNShape`s and edges from `BPMNEdge`s, not by walking
455	`flowElements`. **A node with no shape is invisible; a flow with no edge is
456	dropped.** Generate the full `BPMNDiagram` with `uip maestro bpmn format <file.bpmn>`.
457	
458	- One `<bpmndi:BPMNShape id="S_<nodeId>" bpmnElement="<nodeId>">` per node, with
459	  `<dc:Bounds x= y= width= height= />`. SubProcess shapes carry `isExpanded`.
460	- One `<bpmndi:BPMNEdge id="BPMNEdge_<flowId>" bpmnElement="<flowId>">` per
461	  sequence flow, with `<di:waypoint x= y= />` points.
462	- Lay nodes out left-to-right with non-overlapping bounds. Typical sizes: tasks
463	  100×80, events 36×36, gateways 50×50.
464	
465	Example:
466	
467	```xml
468	<bpmndi:BPMNShape id="S_StartEvent_1" bpmnElement="StartEvent_1">
469	  <dc:Bounds x="160" y="100" width="36" height="36" />
470	</bpmndi:BPMNShape>
471	<bpmndi:BPMNEdge id="BPMNEdge_Flow_1" bpmnElement="Flow_1">
472	  <di:waypoint x="196" y="118" />
473	  <di:waypoint x="260" y="118" />
474	</bpmndi:BPMNEdge>
475	```

478	
479	Safe, surgical edits on an existing `.bpmn` (preserve content you did not author
480	— see [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#editing-an-existing-bpmn-preserve-what-you-did-not-author)):
481	
482	- **Add / delete / reconnect a node**: add the element with a stable id and its
483	  `<bpmn:incoming>`/`<bpmn:outgoing>` refs, add the sequence-flow elements in the
484	  owning scope. On delete, remove orphaned flows and recheck entry-point variables,
485	  output mappings, and binding references. Then regenerate the diagram:
486	  `uip maestro bpmn format <file.bpmn>`. If CLI unavailable: add/update `BPMNShape`
487	  and edge waypoints manually.
488	- **Insert a gateway**: split the existing sequence flow into an incoming and an
489	  outgoing flow, add conditions to the outgoing flows plus one `default`, add a
490	  matching join only if branches actually need synchronization. Then regenerate the
491	  diagram: `uip maestro bpmn format <file.bpmn>`. If CLI unavailable: re-waypoint
492	  manually (gateway shape + all edges).
493	- **Move logic into a subprocess**: move only elements that share a valid scope,
494	  re-scope their variables, recreate legal subprocess flow boundaries, and add a
495	  second diagram plane for the subprocess so nested content renders.
496	- **Add an entry point**: use a root-level start event, add a stable unique
497	  `uipath:entryPointId`, and declare input/output variables whose `elementId`
498	  matches that start event.
499	
500	Do not patch generated JSON to fix source behavior — change the `.bpmn` and
501	regenerate. For `Intsvc.*` activities/triggers, hand editing to CLI enrichment.

1	# Registry workflow
2	
3	Every `uipath:*` payload in a Maestro `.bpmn` comes from the registry — never
4	from prose, never hand-written. This file is the loop for turning user intent
5	into registry-backed XML.
6	
7	## 1. Sync and discover
8	
9	```bash
10	uip maestro bpmn registry pull            # sync + cache (login for connectors/processes)
11	uip maestro bpmn registry list --limit -1 --output json   # all extension types
12	uip maestro bpmn registry search <keyword> --output json  # find a type by intent
13	uip is connections list --all-folders --output json   # live IS connections (all folders)
14	```
15	
16	Map the user's intent to an extension type from the list. Confirm the choice
17	with the user (and the specific connection / process / queue) before authoring.
18	**Never fabricate an identifier** — see [cli-conventions.md](cli-conventions.md).
19	
20	**Connection discovery must be exhaustive.** Always pass `--all-folders` to
21	`uip is connections list` — connections live in many folders and a folder-scoped
22	listing silently misses them. An empty or unmatched result from a missing
23	`--all-folders`, or from a connector key guessed from a brand name rather than
24	found via `registry search`, is a **false negative** — never conclude "no
25	connection exists" or ask the user to create one until you have searched the
26	registry for the real connector key and listed across all folders.
27	
28	`registry list` returns three buckets in `Data`: `ExtensionTypes` (the OOTB
29	extension types, always available), `Connectors` and `Processes` (only after
30	`uip login`). Each extension-type row carries `ExtensionType`, `Label`,
31	`BpmnElement` (the host BPMN element), `ExtensionTag`, and
32	`RequiresDiscovery` (`Yes` means you must resolve a concrete resource — process,
33	queue, connection — before the node is runnable).
34	
35	In temp/smoke sandboxes, a CLI/tooling mismatch can produce valid JSON that is
36	only a failure envelope (for example `"Result": "Failure"`) instead of registry
37	content. For discovery-only tasks, keep that failed output in the transcript or
38	`registry-evidence/cli-error.txt`, then replace the final raw evidence JSON with
39	the matching entries from `validator/bpmn-spec.json`. The final saved evidence
40	must literally contain the requested extension type strings, such as
41	`Orchestrator.StartJob` and `Maestro.ReceiveMessageEvent`, not just the failure
42	envelope.
43	
44	## 2. Get the template for each chosen type
45	
46	```bash
47	uip maestro bpmn registry get <extensionType> --output json
48	```
49	
50	`Data.ExtensionType` contains everything needed to author the node:
51	
52	| Field | Use |
53	| --- | --- |
54	| `xmlTemplate` | The literal node XML with `{placeholder}` slots. **Author from this; fill placeholders only.** |
55	| `bpmnElement` | The host BPMN element the template uses (for source files, normalize to lower-camel such as `bpmn:serviceTask`). |
56	| `extensionTag` | `uipath:activity`, `uipath:event`, or `uipath:mapping`. |
57	| `contextFields[]` | The `uipath:context` inputs; each may carry its own `bindingInfo`. |
58	| `bindingInfo` | How the node binds to a resource (see §4). |
59	| `inputPattern` / `inputName` / `inputTarget` | How the request body input is shaped. |
60	| `requiresDiscovery` / `isDynamic` | Whether a concrete resource must be resolved first. |
61	
62	The placeholders you fill are the obvious ones: `{id}`, `{name}`,
63	`{incomingEdge}`, `{outgoingEdge}`, `{varId}` (the output variable id), plus the
64	per-context-field placeholders (`{releaseKey}`, `{queueName}`, `{appId}`, …) and
65	the body CDATA. Leave the structural placeholders (`{incomingEdge}` /
66	`{outgoingEdge}`) wired to the sequence-flow ids you create in
67	[structural-bpmn.md](structural-bpmn.md).

87	## 4. Bindings — from `bindingInfo`, never invented
88	
89	A node that targets a cloud resource carries a binding. The `bindingInfo` on the
90	extension type tells you the binding shape; the concrete value comes from
91	discovery or the user.
92	
93	- **Resource bindings** (`bindingInfo.resource` = `process` / `queue` /
94	  `businessRule`): the context field named by `bindingInfo.contextField`
95	  (e.g. `releaseKey`, `queueName`) holds the resource key
96	  (`bindingInfo.propertyAttribute`, usually `Key`). Resolve the real key with
97	  `registry search` / discovered `Processes` / `Queues`; never guess a GUID.
98	- **Connection bindings** (`Intsvc.*`): the context references a connection via
99	  `=bindings.<bindingId>`, and a `<uipath:binding>` of `resource="Connection"`
100	  with `propertyAttribute="ConnectionId"` in the process-level
101	  `<uipath:bindings>` holds the live connection id from `uip is connections list`.
102	
103	Declare all bindings in a single process-level `<uipath:bindings version="v1">`
104	block. Each `<uipath:binding>` carries `id`, `resource`, `propertyAttribute`,
105	and a `default` value (the resolved key/id).

107	## Agent wrapper selection — pick by `processType`, not the label
108	
109	When a node invokes an agent, choose the wrapper by the resource's
110	**`processType`** (from `uip or processes list --all-fields`), not its display

113	- Coded Python agents publish as `processType: "Function"` — use the
114	  `Orchestrator.StartJob` process contract, **not** `StartAgentJob`.
115	- Agent Builder (low-code) publishes as `processType: "Agent"` →
116	  `Orchestrator.StartAgentJob`.
117	- External A2A agent addressed by URL / skillId → `A2A.AgentExecution`.
118	- Integration Service external agent → `Intsvc.*AgentExecution`.

123	folder-deployed resources.

125	## API workflow — wait vs fire-and-forget
126	
127	Pick the wrapper by whether downstream needs the invocation result:
128	`Orchestrator.ExecuteApiWorkflow` **waits** for completion (result available to
129	later nodes); `Orchestrator.ExecuteApiWorkflowAsync` **returns immediately**
130	(fire-and-forget). Both are `bpmn:serviceTask` activities. Resolve `ReleaseKey`
131	(process GUID), `FolderKey`/`FolderPath`, and the request/response schemas before
132	the node is runnable — make the wait-versus-async choice explicit in the model.
133	
134	When the caller asks for API workflow invocation/status/result fields, map those
135	fields as `uipath:output` rows on the API workflow `bpmn:serviceTask` itself
136	using the discovered output names/types and `source` expressions, for example
137	`source="=invocation"`, `source="=status"`, and `source="=result"` (or the exact
138	schema fields returned by discovery). Do not add a downstream script task solely
139	to split the API workflow service-task result into variables; that hides the
140	requested service-task output contract from the model.
141	
142	## Integration Service triggers — bind trigger properties via the CLI
143	
144	`Intsvc.TimerTrigger` and `Intsvc.EventTrigger` (and connector waits like
145	`Intsvc.WaitForEvent`) need their **trigger properties** enriched/bound through
146	the CLI — the same enrichment path as `Intsvc.*` activities (§3). A hand-authored
147	trigger shell stays **draft** until the CLI supplies the concrete trigger
148	properties, connection binding, and schemas.
149	
150	## Connectionless vs connector HTTP
151	
152	- **Connector activity** (`Intsvc.ActivityExecution` / a connector-authenticated
153	  operation): use when the call goes through a tenant connection, a dynamic
154	  connector schema, or a connector object operation. Keep the node **draft**
155	  until enriched. The CLI-owned enrichment blockers — the ones that must be
156	  resolved before upload or run, and that boundary notes should name explicitly
157	  — are **connection binding**, **dynamic schemas**, generated **package
158	  metadata** (`bindings_v2.json`, `entry-points.json`, `operate.json`,
159	  `package-descriptor.json`). Do not hand-author any of these (§3).
160	- **Connectionless / manual HTTP** (`Intsvc.HttpExecution`, or
161	  `Intsvc.UnifiedHttpRequest` when current tooling exposes the unified shape):
162	  use when the workflow itself owns the URL, method, payload, and response
163	  parsing (no connection). Author `mode="manual"`, `method`, `url`, `headers`,
164	  `parameters`, `body` directly from the registry template.
165	
166	Status vocabulary for an IS node in a summary: **executable** (activity, inputs,
167	output variable, and downstream mappings present, runtime-verified if a run was
168	done), **draft** (BPMN shape/intent present but enrichment missing), **mock**
169	(returns fixed sample data instead of calling out), **blocked** (a required URL,
170	auth, schema, or enrichment decision is missing).
171	
172	## 5. Assemble
173	
174	1. Build the document scaffold and process (see
175	   [structural-bpmn.md](structural-bpmn.md)).
176	2. Declare root variables (`BPMN.Variables` template) and the
177	   `<uipath:bindings>` block.
178	3. For each node, paste its `registry get` `xmlTemplate`, fill placeholders, and
179	   wire `{incomingEdge}`/`{outgoingEdge}` to your sequence flows.
180	4. Author the structural BPMN the registry does not emit: sequence flows,
181	   gateway conditions/defaults, event definitions, boundary events,
182	   subprocess/call-activity containers, multi-instance markers.
183	5. Generate the `bpmndi:BPMNDiagram`: `uip maestro bpmn format <file.bpmn>`
184	6. Validate (see [structural-bpmn.md#validation](structural-bpmn.md#validation)).
185	
186	## OOTB extension types (29, login-free)
187	
188	These are the built-in types `registry pull` returns without login. Discover the
189	exact template for any of them with `registry get <type>`.
190	
191	| Extension type | Host element | Tag |
192	| --- | --- | --- |
193	| `Actions.HITL` | `bpmn:userTask` | activity |
194	| `Orchestrator.StartJob` | `bpmn:serviceTask` | activity |
195	| `Orchestrator.StartAgentJob` | `bpmn:serviceTask` | activity |
196	| `Orchestrator.BusinessRules` | `bpmn:businessRuleTask` | activity |
197	| `Orchestrator.ExecuteApiWorkflowAsync` | `bpmn:serviceTask` | activity |
198	| `Orchestrator.CreateQueueItem` | `bpmn:sendTask` | activity |
199	| `Orchestrator.CreateAndWaitForQueueItem` | `bpmn:serviceTask` | activity |
200	| `Orchestrator.StartAgenticProcess[Async]` | `bpmn:callActivity` | activity |
201	| `Orchestrator.StartCaseMgmtProcess[Async]` | `bpmn:callActivity` | activity |
202	| `Intsvc.ActivityExecution` | `bpmn:sendTask` | activity |
203	| `Intsvc.HttpExecution` / `Intsvc.UnifiedHttpRequest` | `bpmn:sendTask` | activity |
204	| `Intsvc.WaitForEvent` | `bpmn:receiveTask` | event |
205	| `Intsvc.EventTrigger` | `bpmn:startEvent` | event |
206	| `Intsvc.TimerTrigger` | `bpmn:startEvent` | activity |
207	| `Intsvc.{Async,SyncAgent,AsyncAgent,SyncWorkflow,AsyncWorkflow}Execution` | `bpmn:serviceTask` | activity |
208	| `A2A.AgentExecution` | `bpmn:serviceTask` | activity |
209	| `BPMN.Variables` | `bpmn:task` | mapping |
210	| `BPMN.ScriptTask` | `bpmn:scriptTask` | mapping |
211	| `Maestro.ReceiveMessageEvent` | `bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent` | event |
212	| `Maestro.SendMessageEvent` | `bpmn:intermediateThrowEvent` | event |
213	| `Maestro.CaseRulesEvaluator` / `Maestro.CaseManagerGuardrails` | `bpmn:serviceTask` | activity |
214	
215	This table is a discovery aid, not a substitute for `registry get` — always pull
216	the live template before authoring.
217	
218	If a registry `xmlTemplate` returns a PascalCase BPMN host tag such as
219	`bpmn:SendTask` or `bpmn:ReceiveTask`, normalize only the BPMN host element

1	# Project Layout
2	
3	Maestro BPMN Process Orchestration projects use BPMN XML as source and generated JSON files as package/runtime metadata.
4	
5	## Canonical source files
6	
7	- `<project>.bpmn` - BPMN process source and UiPath extension XML. For a new
8	  project, keep the BPMN source basename exactly aligned with the project
9	  directory/name. For example, `InvoiceTriageBpmn/InvoiceTriageBpmn.bpmn`, not
10	  `InvoiceTriageBpmn/invoice-triage-bpmn.bpmn`.
11	- `project.uiproj` - UiPath project metadata. Keep it in the same project
12	  directory as the main BPMN file: `InvoiceTriageBpmn/project.uiproj`, not next
13	  to the project directory.
14	
15	For a new local project, place source files under a single project directory.
16	`uip maestro bpmn init <ProjectName> --output json` nests that directory inside
17	a solution. Inside a solution it registers the project with the parent `.uipx`;
18	outside any solution it auto-scaffolds `<ProjectName>Solution/` and nests the
19	project inside (the response adds `Data.AutoCreatedSolution` =
20	`{ Name, Path, SolutionFile }` and reports `SolutionRegistration.Status:
21	Registered`; re-running is idempotent and reports `AlreadyRegistered`):
22	
23	```text
24	ProjectNameSolution/             ← auto-scaffolded when init runs outside a solution
25	  ProjectNameSolution.uipx
26	  ProjectName/
27	    ProjectName.bpmn
28	    project.uiproj
29	```
30	
31	With `--skip-solution-registration`, the project lands bare instead, with no
32	solution wrapper:
33	
34	```text
35	ProjectName/
36	  ProjectName.bpmn
37	  project.uiproj
38	```
39	
40	If a **non-empty** directory already exists at the path you typed, init warns
41	and leaves it untouched — the project still lands in
42	`<ProjectName>Solution/<ProjectName>/`, not the existing directory.
43	
44	## Generated or CLI-managed package files
45	
46	- `bindings_v2.json` - resource bindings generated or enriched from BPMN and registry/connection metadata.
47	- `entry-points.json` - runnable start-event entry points and input/output schemas.
48	- `operate.json` - runtime/package metadata.
49	- `package-descriptor.json` - package manifest mapping generated files and BPMN content.
50	
51	Treat these JSON files as derived unless a CLI contract explicitly identifies a field as user-authored. For source fixes, edit BPMN or rerun CLI enrichment rather than patching generated output by hand.
52	
53	Local packaging requires the generated metadata set to exist. In particular,
54	`uip maestro bpmn pack <project-path> <OutputDir> --output json` consumes
55	`package-descriptor.json`; it does not create a missing descriptor from only
56	the BPMN and `project.uiproj`.
57	
58	For the regeneration and drift-check contract, see [local-metadata-regeneration-guide.md](local-metadata-regeneration-guide.md).
59	
60	## Package content
61	
62	A synthetic local project authored without a CLI generator must still match the
63	executable and metadata contract before packing: the BPMN root process includes
64	`isExecutable="true"`, `project.uiproj` has lowercase `"main"`,
65	`operate.json` has `"main"` plus `"contentType": "ProcessOrchestration"`, and
66	`package-descriptor.json` has top-level `"content"` entries under `content/`.
67	For the exact minimal JSON, see
68	[local-metadata-regeneration-guide.md](local-metadata-regeneration-guide.md#minimal-local-metadata-shape).
69	
70	A Process Orchestration package content folder contains:
71	
72	- One or more `.bpmn` files.
73	- `bindings_v2.json`.
74	- `entry-points.json`.
75	- `operate.json`.
76	- `package-descriptor.json`.
77	
78	The package descriptor maps BPMN and generated JSON files under `content/`. The entry point file path references the BPMN file and start event, using the root start event's unique entry point ID.
79	
80	## Authoring boundary
81	
82	Authoring owns local files and local validation. It can create or edit BPMN source, preserve existing generated files for comparison, and run validation/generation commands. It stops before upload, debug, publish, or run unless the user explicitly consents.
83	
84	Operate owns cloud-side side effects: upload, publish, deploy, debug, process run, instance lifecycle, and cloud resource refresh.
85	
86	Diagnose owns post-run inspection: incidents, variables, element executions, deployed assets, traces, and correlation back to BPMN element IDs.

1	# CLI Conventions (authoring)
2	
3	This reference covers the **authoring-side** CLI surface only: the read-only
4	registry discovery commands used to produce a valid, importable Maestro `.bpmn`
5	file. The registry commands below never mutate cloud state. Operate and diagnose
6	use different CLI commands — see
7	[operate/CAPABILITY.md](operate/CAPABILITY.md) and
8	[diagnose/CAPABILITY.md](diagnose/CAPABILITY.md).
9	
10	## Discovery commands (read-only, authoring-safe)
11	
12	All commands below are discovery/read-only. None mutate cloud state.
13	
14	| Command | Purpose |
15	| --- | --- |
16	| `uip maestro bpmn registry pull [-f\|--force]` | Sync and cache the registry. Without login, only OOTB extension types are synced; login adds discovered connectors and processes. |
17	| `uip maestro bpmn registry list [--limit <n\|-1>]` | List cached extension types (and discovered connectors/processes). Default 30; use `--limit -1` for all. |
18	| `uip maestro bpmn registry search <keyword>` | Find entries by keyword across extension type, label, connector name, process name. |
19	| `uip maestro bpmn registry get <extensionType> [--connection-id <id>] [--object-name <name>]` | Get the full spec for one extension type: `xmlTemplate`, `contextFields`, `bindingInfo`, input/output patterns. `--connection-id`/`--object-name` add live Integration Service field metadata for `Intsvc.*` connector types. |
20	| `uip is connections list --all-folders` | List live Integration Service connections (id + state) across all folders. Always pass `--all-folders`; a folder-scoped list silently misses connections. |
21	
22	These are the registry/discovery commands the skill verifies against the CLI
23	source (`packages/maestro-tool/src/commands/registry.ts`). Do not invent flags.
24	Validation uses `uip maestro bpmn validate <file>` — see
25	[Validation](structural-bpmn.md#validation).
26	
27	The `validate` command runs the full PO.Frontend canvas rule set offline (it was
28	added to the CLI in UiPath/cli#3135). If your CLI reports `validate` as an
29	unknown command, or it clearly runs only the deploy-readiness checks and not the
30	structural rules, the installed CLI predates that change — update to the latest:
31	
32	```bash
33	npm install -g @uipath/cli@latest   # or: bun add -g @uipath/cli
34	```
35	
36	> **Don't conclude "it doesn't exist" from truncated discovery output.** A row past a cutoff reads exactly like a missing row. Two cutoffs bite here: `registry list` defaults to **30** — pass `--limit -1` for the full set — and piping `registry search`/`is connections list` through `head`/`tail`/`grep -m`/a pager drops everything past the cap. To check existence, narrow the query (keyword to `registry search`, `--all-folders` to connection lists) rather than capping rows; cap only data already known complete.
37	
38	## Output parsing
39	
40	Whenever a CLI result is parsed programmatically, pass `--output json`. If a
41	command does not support JSON, do not silently scrape human text; keep the step
42	manual and tell the user.
43	
44	## Login boundary
45	
46	Local source authoring and `uip maestro bpmn validate` work without login (the
47	validator runs fully offline). Registry
48	discovery of **connectors and processes** (and Integration Service field
49	enrichment) requires `uip login`. Without login, `registry pull` still returns
50	the built-in (OOTB) extension types.
51	
52	## Never fabricate an identifier
53	
54	Connection IDs, `releaseKey`/process keys, queue keys, connector keys, app IDs,
55	folder IDs/paths — every concrete identifier comes from discovery
56	(`registry get`, `registry search`, `uip is connections list`) or from the user.
57	Never invent one. When a required identifier is unknown, leave the placeholder
58	in place, flag it as a draft binding, and ask the user.

1	# Local Metadata Regeneration
2	
3	Use this guide when BPMN source changed and local package metadata must be refreshed or verified before packaging, upload, debug, publish, or deploy.
4	
5	## Ownership
6	
7	- `.bpmn` is the source of record for process structure, root variables, root bindings, entry point IDs, mappings, diagrams, and documented non-Integration-Service UiPath XML.
8	- `entry-points.json`, `bindings_v2.json`, `operate.json`, and `package-descriptor.json` are derived package metadata unless a CLI contract explicitly marks a field as user-authored.
9	- Connector-backed or dynamically schematized `Intsvc.*` activity and event payloads are executable only after registry-backed enrichment supplies connector metadata, connection binding references, dynamic schemas, and generated package resources. Confirmed plain connectionless HTTP follows the documented pass-2 authoring recipe instead.
10	
11	## Local Synthetic Project Contract
12	
13	When no CLI generator is available and you must author a local-only synthetic
14	BPMN project, make the project executable and package-shaped before packing:
15	
16	- The root process must be `<bpmn:process ... isExecutable="true">`.
17	- `project.uiproj` must use lowercase `"main"` pointing at the BPMN file.
18	- `operate.json` must use `"main"` with the bare BPMN filename, not a
19	  `/content/<file>.bpmn#<start-event-id>` entry-point path, plus
20	  `"contentType": "ProcessOrchestration"`.
21	- `package-descriptor.json` must use a top-level `"content"` array with
22	  `content/<file>` entries. Do not use `contentFiles` or a CLI scaffold
23	  `"files"` mapping for synthetic local metadata.
24	
25	The minimal placeholder-safe JSON shape is shown below; keep it exact apart
26	from project, file, and start event names.
27	
28	## Regeneration Inputs
29	
30	Local regeneration reads:
31	
32	- Root-level `bpmn:startEvent` elements with `uipath:entryPointId`.
33	- Root `uipath:variables` for entry point input/output schemas.
34	- Root `uipath:bindings` for package resources.
35	- Enriched `uipath:activity` and `uipath:event` payloads for `Intsvc.*` context fields, request payloads, output mappings, and schemas.
36	- The project main file from `project.uiproj` or the selected BPMN file.
37	
38	Do not derive metadata from stale package files first. Use existing generated files only as a drift comparison or as CLI-owned enrichment input when the CLI explicitly supports that workflow.
39	
40	## Safe Local Workflow
41	
42	1. Edit `.bpmn` first.
43	2. Run local validation for XML, diagrams, entry point IDs, variables, mappings, binding references, and package metadata drift.
44	3. Regenerate package metadata from the BPMN source:
45	
46	   ```bash
47	   uip maestro bpmn update-metadata <file.bpmn> --dry-run   # check drift
48	   uip maestro bpmn update-metadata <file.bpmn>             # regenerate
49	   ```
50	
51	   If CLI unavailable for a local-only synthetic project, write the minimal
52	   placeholder-safe shape (see below) before continuing.
53	
54	4. Verify the project directory now contains the full metadata set:
55	   `project.uiproj`, `operate.json`, `entry-points.json`, `bindings_v2.json`,
56	   and `package-descriptor.json`. The pack command consumes these files; it does
57	   not synthesize a missing package descriptor.

142	## Entry Point Rules
143	
144	For each root start event with `uipath:entryPointId`, generated `entry-points.json` must include:
145	
146	- `id` equal to the `uipath:entryPointId` value.
147	- `filePath` equal to `/content/<bpmn-file>#<start-event-id>`.
148	- `inputSchema` from root input variables whose `elementId` matches the start event.
149	- `outputSchema` from root output variables.
150	
151	JSON schema variables use their CDATA body as the property schema. Strip `$schema` from generated package schemas. Other primitive variables map by type, such as `string`, `integer`, `number`, `boolean`, `array`, `object`, or `json`.
152	
153	## Binding Rules
154	
155	Generated `bindings_v2.json` must be a top-level object with
156	`"version": "2.0"` and a `resources` array. Do not use a bare resource array, a
157	single resource object, or an unversioned `{ "resources": [] }` object; those
158	shapes are not the package contract consumed by solution resources refresh.
159	
160	The resource array has two consumers with different tolerance:
161	
162	- Local/package binding expressions may need id-addressable entries that mirror
163	  root `uipath:binding` IDs.
164	- `uip solution resources refresh` reads the same `resources` array and imports
165	  concrete dependencies only when it contains parseable resource entries.
166	  Process resources should come from CLI generation or fixture-backed binding
167	  entries with `id`, `kind`, `name`, `resourceKey`, `metadata`, `resource`,
168	  `resourceSubType`, and, for name/folder-path binding pairs,
169	  `propertyAttribute`.
170	
171	When an executable BPMN depends on remote Orchestrator processes, include
172	generated process binding resources before refresh so it can import the
173	process/package resources and write debug overwrites. If resource dependencies
174	are expected, verify that refresh produced matching generated resource files or
175	explicitly report that no dependency resources were imported.
176	
177	Generated id-addressable entries should preserve:
178	
179	- `id`, `name`, kind/type, and `resourceKey`.
180	- `metadata.BindingsVersion` for the source binding version.
181	- `metadata.DisplayLabel` from the binding display name.
182	- `metadata.SubType` from the binding resource subtype or type.
183	- Connector metadata, parent resource keys, and solution support fields supplied by Integration Service enrichment.
184	
185	If multiple BPMN elements share a connector connection binding, regenerate or validate deduplication through the CLI instead of copying a resource entry by hand.
186	
187	## Integration Service Enrichment
188	
189	Before a connector element is executable, enrichment must make these fields agree:
190	
191	- Every `Intsvc.*` `connection`, `trigger`, object/property, or resource context value references an existing root binding with `=bindings.<id>`.
192	- The referenced package resource exists in `bindings_v2.json`.
193	- Connector-specific package metadata agrees with the `connectorKey` in the enriched payload.
194	- Trigger property resources carry the parent trigger resource key when required by the connector shape.
195	- Activity payloads include required operation context and generated request/input schema data when the selected operation requires it.
196	- Output mappings target declared variables and dynamic output schemas are generated by the enrichment tool.
197	
198	If enrichment is unavailable, leave the BPMN element as draft intent. Do not hand-author real connection IDs, tenant resource keys, connector payloads, or dynamic schemas.
199	
200	## Drift Handling
201	
202	- If `entry-points.json` differs from root variables or start event IDs, fix the BPMN source first, then regenerate.
203	- If `bindings_v2.json` differs from root bindings or `Intsvc.*` context references, rerun enrichment/generation.
204	- If `operate.json` or `package-descriptor.json` points at the wrong BPMN file, refresh package metadata through the CLI path.
205	- Do not commit private IDs, tenant URLs, connection IDs, folder keys, or copied customer payloads while resolving drift.

1	# Expression Authoring
2	
3	Use this reference whenever pass 2 writes Maestro runtime expressions in BPMN
4	XML. Pass 1 may use business-readable placeholder conditions; pass 2 replaces
5	them with expressions only after the variables and scopes exist.
6	
7	## Stored expression shape
8	
9	- Use a leading `=` where Maestro expects expression content.
10	- Treat values without `=` as literals.
11	- Read BPMN variables through `vars.<variableId>`, for example
12	  `=vars.Var_RequestId`.
13	- Do not use bare variable names such as `=requestId` in generated runtime XML.
14	- Context bindings use `=bindings.<bindingId>`.
15	- Current element outputs use `result` only in output mappings for that
16	  element. For new BPMN script tasks, return an object and expose its value
17	  through `result.response`: use `return { response: value };` with
18	  `source="=result.response"` for a scalar variable, or return a nested object
19	  and use `source="=result.response.<field>"` for a field. Do not use
20	  `source="=result"` with a bare scalar return in live debug/runtime BPMN; the
21	  run can complete while the mapped variable reads back empty.
22	- Multi-instance task bodies read the current item from `iterator.item`.
23	- Multi-instance subprocess bodies read the current item from
24	  `iterator[0].item`. Use `iterator[1].item` (and so on) inside nested
25	  multi-instance subprocesses: the index counts nesting depth from outermost
26	  (`[0]`) to innermost.
27	- The current 0-based loop index inside any multi-instance body is exposed as
28	  `iterator.loopCounter` for tasks and `iterator[N].loopCounter` for
29	  subprocesses at depth N.
30	- Error mapping conditions may inspect the built-in error object through
31	  `vars.error`, for example `=vars.error.code == "SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE"`.
32	
33	## Inline JavaScript with `=js:`
34	
35	When a mapping body or context value needs computation that a simple
36	`=vars.<id>` expression cannot express, prefix the body with `=js:` and follow
37	it with a JavaScript expression. The runtime evaluates the rest of the value
38	against the same `vars`, `bindings`, `result`, and `iterator` namespaces.
39	Use this form inside CDATA mapping bodies; it is the runtime-supported
40	escape hatch the BPMN expression grammar does not otherwise expose.
41	
42	```xml
43	<uipath:input name="JobArguments" type="json" target="bodyField"><![CDATA[
44	{"startRow":"=js:iterator[0].loopCounter * vars.Var_RowsPerShard",
45	 "endRow":"=js:(iterator[0].loopCounter + 1) * vars.Var_RowsPerShard - 1"}
46	]]></uipath:input>
47	```
48	
49	Rules:
50	
51	- The prefix is `=js:` (case-sensitive, no space).
52	- The body must still satisfy lint-sensitive constraints: no assignment
53	  operators in fields where read-only expressions are required.
54	- Prefer plain `=vars.<id>` or `=bindings.<id>` when the value does not need
55	  computation — `=js:` should be reserved for arithmetic, string
56	  manipulation, or conditional selection.
57	- A `=js:` expression that returns an object or array must produce valid JSON
58	  for fields typed `json`.
59	
60	Prefer JavaScript-safe variable ids such as `Var_RequestId`. If a brownfield
61	file contains non-identifier ids, preserve them and let the product editor or
62	CLI normalize the access form; do not silently rename variables without updating
63	all mappings, expressions, and generated metadata.
64	
65	## Lint-sensitive fields
66	
67	These fields must be read-only expressions:
68	
69	- Gateway `bpmn:conditionExpression` values.
70	- Activity skip conditions.
71	- Multi-instance completion and filter conditions.
72	- `uipath:errorMapping` condition values.
73	- Mapping values that read variables or element outputs.
74	
75	Do not use assignment operators in these fields. Comparisons such as `==`,
76	`===`, `!=`, `!==`, `>=`, and `<=` are allowed.
77	
78	## Scope and availability
79	
80	- Root variables are visible across the root process after they are declared and
81	  reachable by control flow.
82	- An output variable you intend to expose in runtime inspection (via
83	  `debug-instance variables-all` or `instance variables`) must be root-scoped —
84	  declare its `uipath:output` or `uipath:inputOutput` WITHOUT an `elementId`. A
85	  variable scoped with `elementId` is bound to that element and is not surfaced
86	  as a root/global runtime variable. Preserve exact variable ids: if the
87	  requested variable id is `product`, declare `id="product"` and map to
88	  `var="product"`, not `Product` or `Var_Product`. Current BPMN live debug may
89	  expose the root output definition while still returning the value as `null`;
90	  treat that as a runtime/debug API limitation, not proof that the authored
91	  mapping is absent.
92	- Subprocess variables stay scoped to that subprocess.
93	- Output mappings should target `uipath:inputOutput` or `uipath:output`
94	  variables, not read-only `uipath:input` variables.
95	- Entry point inputs that must later be updated need a separate mutable
96	  `uipath:inputOutput` variable and an explicit mapping from the entry input.
97	- Trigger-bound values are commonly represented as `uipath:inputOutput`
98	  variables scoped with `elementId` so the trigger can write them during
99	  execution.
100	
101	## Common mistakes
102	
103	- `=requestId` instead of `=vars.Var_RequestId`.
104	- `var="requestId"` instead of `var="Var_RequestId"`.
105	- Using `result` outside the output mapping of the element that produced it.
106	- Reading `iterator[0].item` outside the multi-instance subprocess body.
107	- Moving a variable into a subprocess without updating mappings that read it
108	  from the root scope.

1	# Public Safety
2	
3	This skill is intended for a public skills repository. Keep all content, examples, fixtures, logs, and commits safe to publish.
4	
5	## Never include
6	
7	- Raw exported BPMN from customers, tenants, demos, or operator-supplied examples.
8	- Tenant URLs, organization names, folder keys, connection IDs, release keys, queue IDs, process IDs, user IDs, or email addresses.
9	- Private process names, business payloads, screenshots, exported package contents, or traces.
10	- Local absolute paths from developer machines.
11	- Temporary mission notes, task transcripts, or Rookery-only context.
12	- Internal-only repository paths as runtime instructions for the skill user.
13	
14	## Use instead
15	
16	- Synthetic process names such as `InvoiceApproval`.
17	- Synthetic element IDs such as `Task_ValidateRequest`.
18	- Placeholder resource labels such as `<PROCESS_NAME>`, `<FOLDER_KEY>`, or `<CONNECTION_NAME>` when the user must provide a real value.
19	- Short structural examples that demonstrate XML shape without private data.
20	- Summaries of behavior rather than copied private XML.
21	
22	## XML placeholder escaping
23	
24	Angle-bracket placeholders are safe only when the XML location can contain text
25	or CDATA. In XML attributes, escape the brackets so the BPMN remains
26	well-formed:
27	
28	- Attribute values: `value="<TENANT_URL>"`,
29	  `value="<FOLDER_KEY>"`, `value="<CONNECTION_NAME>"`.
30	- Element text or CDATA: `<TENANT_URL>`, `<FOLDER_KEY>`, and
31	  `<CONNECTION_NAME>` may be used as literal placeholder text.
32	
33	After sanitizing a BPMN file, parse it before reporting done. A sanitization
34	pass that replaces a private value with unescaped `<PLACEHOLDER>` inside an
35	attribute has made the file invalid.
36	
37	## Review checklist
38	
39	Before committing:
40	
41	- Search changed files for local path fragments, URLs, IDs, and private names.
42	- Confirm every example can be understood without access to internal repositories.
43	- Confirm Integration Service examples do not contain real connector resource identifiers.
